items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...was the Thad Jones - Mel Lewis Band. And she did an album that was just killing. [INTERVIEWEE] It really was. It still is.

ctx.x: She told us some stories about traveling that were, something else.
And she did an album with one of the greatest jazz bands in the history of this country as far as I was concerned, was the Thad Jones - Mel Lewis Band. And she did an album that was just killing.
It really was. It still is.

items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I made several tours, at least two tours of Europe and two tours of the Far East with Jones, or maybe I’m confusing with the Thad Jones – Mel Lewis Orchestra.

ctx.x: He formed his own group, the Jazz Machine. I was on and off with that group from about ’69 on through the mid ’70s. I made several tours, at least two tours of Europe and two tours of the Far East with Jones, or maybe I’m confusing with the Thad Jones – Mel Lewis Orchestra. I made at least one tour of Japan with Elvin, one tour of South America, and one tour of Europe. That’s a playing experience that any saxophonist would treasure, would feel that something was missed if they didn’t play with Elvin at least one…
